To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can train interpretable recommender systems by feeding Factorization Machines with knowledge graph information.
the proposed approach is capable to improve the interpretability of a recommender system model, by using a knowledge graph as a source of semantic features.

(i) we show that the use of semantic features in the initialization of a Factorization Machine model can improve the accuracy of the recommendation process, (ii) the knowledge graph used to initialize the model can improve the interpretability of the model itself, (iii) the knowledge graph can improve the robustness of the model in terms of semantic accuracy, and (iv) the use of semantic information can improve the interpretablility and robustness of a Factorization Machines model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can we make a model interpretable by feeding it with semantic information? The answer is yes.
the problem of making interpretable the latent space of a recommender system model.
the development of a new approach to knowledge-aware recommendation, which can be easily integrated in any model based recommendation system.

we are able to train a model with the same level of accuracy of the original FM model, while retaining the interpretability of the knowledge graph.
the proposed model is able to improve the accuracy of recommendations and, at the same time, to provide a more interpretable model.
we have proposed an approach to make the latent factors of a model interpretable by using a knowledge graph.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by using knowledge graphs, it is possible to train a model that can provide accurate and interpretable recommendations.
we show how to train a knowledge aware Factorization Machine model, which is interpretable, accurate, and robust.
we are able to learn an interpretable model that can recommend items and, at the same time, can explain why a specific item has been recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to train a model that is both accurate and interpretable by using a simple and efficient approach.
the use of knowledge graphs is a powerful tool for improving the accuracy and the interpretability of recommender systems.
